CNBC reports the Fed pointed to a hike in March [[n2089]], so the debate is size. December inflation rose 7%, the highest since 1982, per CNBC [[n1961]], and the 2Y at 1.31% has risen 43 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04). CME Group lays out rate-hike expectations against reality [[n2114]], while Reuters argues a big-bang start is not likely [[n2139]].
Conditional Expression

If the next CPI print runs hot, the cleanest expression is further front-end weakness and a flatter curve: stay short the 2Y and long XLF against XLRE. If it surprises softer, the bear flattening should unwind first at the 2Y, favouring a tactical rebound in the Nasdaq 100, still -6.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), and in rate-sensitive real estate.
Risk

Inflation is not the only driver. A geopolitical shock could pull yields down even with a hot print, turning a short-duration position into a loser. Wages are the persistence test; Apricitas Economics asks what is going on with wages [[n2135]], and a fast wage trend would keep the Fed hawkish whatever the monthly CPI does.

anticipatory.title: Russia-Ukraine: diplomacy against a pending invasion risk
parts: What Is Priced

Oil and gas carry the premium; equities carry little. Brent is +13.76% over 20 sessions to 93.27 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), and Reuters reports strategists see oil hitting $100 [[n1389]]. NBC reports nerves fraying at the Ukraine border as Russian troops mass in Belarus [[n1411]], and the Economist says America is preparing the mother of all sanctions [[n1404]].
Conditional Expression

POLITICO reports Macron heading east on a risky peacemaker mission [[n1280]]. If diplomacy gains traction, fade the oil premium through energy against the market and add European cyclicals such as autos, with the SXAP tracker -8.36% over 20 sessions at 59.27 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). If invasion risk escalates, own energy, defence and Treasuries, and cut Polish and euro-area banks.
Risk

Sanctions may spare energy flows. The Japan Times notes Putin's financial fortress blunts the impact of threatened sanctions [[n1391]], so even an escalation might not deliver the physical supply shock oil is pricing, leaving long-energy positions exposed to a sharp reversal.

anticipatory.title: Poland's February MPC decision
parts: What Is Priced

Pekao expects the Monetary Policy Council to raise rates by 50 bps in February [[n1706]], and bank shares already reflect higher rates, with Pekao +8.56% over 20 sessions at 134.40 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Money.pl notes Czech rates are twice as high as Poland's [[n1683]], a gap that keeps pressure on the NBP to catch up.
Conditional Expression

A hike in line with Pekao's call keeps the bank overweight intact. A larger move or hawkish guidance would favour PKO BP and mBank further and could stabilise the zloty, which helps importers such as LPP. A smaller move would hit the currency and the banks together, the worst outcome for Polish exposure.
Risk

Business Insider Polska argues a clear fall in inflation is entirely in Glapiński's hands [[n1582]]. If the NBP under-delivers, inflation expectations rise, real rates fall further, and the bank trade becomes a currency trade that foreign holders can exit quickly.

anticipatory.title: China's reopening and the next easing step
parts: What Is Priced

Hong Kong has priced a policy-led recovery. The Hang Seng rose +3.24% on reopening and Tencent is +9.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), while the Shanghai Composite's last close of 3,361.44 index points still reflects the -7.12% pre-holiday slide (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28).
Conditional Expression

If mainland shares open firm and the central bank adds easing, ASHR, at 36.53 USD and -3.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), is the catch-up trade against FXI. If the services survey disappoints or property news worsens, Hong Kong's gains are vulnerable and Australian miners such as Fortescue, +9.72% over five sessions to 21.34 AUD, would give back their China premium.
Risk

Zero-COVID cuts both ways: the New York Times reports China's strict virus policy has left fruit abandoned [[n0235]], a reminder that lockdowns hit supply and consumption together. The Asia Times frames an Olympian Soros-versus-Dalio debate on China [[n0230]]; with positioning this split, a disappointment could move prices sharply.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Meta Platforms (FB) closed at 237.09 USD, -21.42% over five sessions and -28.69% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). CNBC reports Facebook says Apple's iOS privacy change will mean a $10 billion revenue hit this year [[n0540]], and CNBC says the metaverse business lost more than $10 billion last year, with losses still growing [[n1061]]. The thesis: a de-rating from compounder to capital-intensive turnaround.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Recovery needs stable daily users; Business Insider reports Zuckerberg citing unprecedented competition from TikTok [[n1127]]. The risk to the bearish stance is valuation: Business Insider notes Meta sank below Berkshire Hathaway in market value for the first time in nearly two years [[n0688]], inviting value buyers.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; prefer Alphabet for advertising exposure. Revisit only if measurement fixes restore ad pricing and the stock holds above 237.09 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04).

catalysts.title: Amazon (AMZN)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Amazon closed at 3,152.79 USD, +13.54% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), a jump Bloomberg calls a record $191 billion gain in market value [[n0107]]. GeekWire reports Amazon would have posted a $1.8 billion Q4 operating loss without AWS [[n0635]], and CNBC sizes its advertising business at $31 billion a year [[n1088]]. The thesis: cloud, ads and Prime pricing now fund retail.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The 20-session change is still -3.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), a partial recovery. Reuters cites rising wages and costs behind the Prime fee hike [[n1089]], and Bloomberg says a Peloton deal may pose a regulatory headache for a tech giant [[n0866]].
Trade Expression
Own, and add if the stock holds most of Friday's +13.54% gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04) through the week. Exit if AWS growth decelerates or Prime churn rises.

catalysts.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Exxon closed at 81.41 USD, +8.14% over five sessions and +19.16% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). The New York Times reports an $8.9 billion fourth-quarter profit as oil prices soared [[n0402]], MarketWatch says Exxon will merge chemicals and refining in a cost-cutting reorganisation [[n0405]], and World Oil reports it joining Chevron in a Permian surge [[n1010]]. The thesis: cash returns plus volume growth.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Brent at 93.27 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04) already discounts much of the war premium. Reuters reports the US restored a sanctions waiver to Iran with nuclear talks in a final phase [[n1398]]; a deal, or Ukraine de-escalation, would cut the price that funds buybacks.
Trade Expression
Hold core and add on pullbacks while WTI keeps its +16.17% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04); reduce if Brent loses its +13.76%.

catalysts.title: PayPal (PYPL)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

PayPal closed at 126.08 USD, -22.90% over five sessions and -34.43% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Payments Dive reports PayPal scrapped its account growth goal [[n0579]], and Forbes says it admitted 4.5 million accounts were illegitimate as fintech's fraud problem grows [[n1068]]. The thesis: user growth, the core of the valuation, has stalled.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The bear case has a credible counterweight: Wolfe Research's Darrin Peller tells CNBC he believes there will be consistency to PayPal's growth [[n0482]]. Any stabilising engagement metric could force a sharp short-covering rally from depressed levels.
Trade Expression

Avoid; prefer Visa, 228.39 USD and +3.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), for payments exposure. Revisit only if management restores a credible account target and engagement stabilises.

catalysts.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AMD closed at 123.60 USD, +17.45% over five sessions but -9.27% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). CNBC reports CEO Lisa Su says AMD grew in every business [[n1036]], and Notebookcheck says AMD expects record 2022 earnings and is closing in on Intel's profit margins [[n1037]]. The thesis is continuing share gains against a stumbling incumbent.
Price Hurdle & Risk

SOXX is -11.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), so a renewed rate spike would hit semis first. Intel, -11.11% over 20 sessions, shows how fast sentiment can turn, and AMD's valuation leaves less room for an execution miss.
Trade Expression
Own AMD against Intel as a pair. Add on a move back above the 20-session reference close of 136.23 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04); cut if the stock surrenders its post-results gain.

catalysts.title: Ford Motor (F)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Ford closed at 17.96 USD, -9.70% on Friday and -26.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Reuters reports Ford will suspend or cut output at 8 of its factories due to the chip shortage [[n0779]], and, citing Bloomberg News, a new investment of up to $20 billion in its EV push [[n0542]]. The thesis: a credible EV story held back by chips.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The New York Times says 2021 profit was bolstered by a large Rivian gain [[n0660]], overstating core earnings. Fox Business reports CEO Farley is cracking down hard on $3.6 billion of dealer markups [[n1142]], a brand-protection step that does nothing for near-term volumes.
Trade Expression

Wait for chip-supply evidence before buying the dip. GM's forecast of earnings at or near record levels in 2022 [[n0416]] makes it the better near-term auto exposure; Ford is the recovery trade later.

spec.retail_intro: The crowd's dominant story is the results-day rescue, the belief that a growth stock priced for disaster can reprice in one session, with last year's GameStop saga as the template even though these gaps are earnings-driven, not squeezes.

retail.title: Snap / SNAP — the survivor of the Facebook crash
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Snap is the trade of the weekend because it lets the crowd tell itself the cleanest story in tech: Facebook broke, the little yellow app did not. A day after Meta's 26% plunge, its biggest one-day drop ever [[n0658]], Snap closed at 38.91 USD, up 58.82% in a single session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Barron's called it the stock's best day ever and argued it doesn't have all of Facebook's problems [[n0817]]. The hook is the comeback with a side of schadenfreude: the Apple privacy change that the New York Times says is tormenting internet companies, especially Meta [[n0624]], hung over every social-ad stock, and the underdog drew TechCrunch's headline 'Snap finally did it, y'all' [[n1121]]. It feels obvious because the scoreboard is so loud.
What Is Driving It

The backdrop explains the violence. Meta had told investors Apple's iOS privacy change will mean a $10 billion revenue hit this year [[n0540]], and Facebook's user numbers shrank for the first time in its history [[n1102]]; Meta Platforms closed at 237.09 USD, down 21.42% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Snap reported into a sector already marked for that scenario, so the relief was concentrated: its five-session gain is 27.91%, and Pinterest, whose results Reuters said dazzled Wall Street [[n0703]], added 11.18% to 27.25 USD the same day. The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.33% to 14,694.35 index points as the Nasdaq ended a choppy week higher [[n0227]]. The tension is rates: the 2-year Treasury yield sits at 1.31%, up 43 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-04).
The Social Signal

The attention trail is unusually explicit. On Moomoo, the retail brokerage platform, an item titled “‘Snap’ your fingers and gain 50% profit within a day! WOW!” [[n0876]] captures the mood: the trade is being pitched as a jackpot, not as an ad-market thesis. The Ankler's 'SNAP stock pops 60%' [[n0815]] carried the number beyond finance audiences, while USA Today told readers that Facebook's plunge brings big losses for Zuckerberg, Meta 'and maybe you' [[n0736]]. When a loss story and a jackpot story land side by side, the crowd tends to rotate from the casualty to the survivor.
Historical Analog

The template is a year old. The GameStop saga taught traders that one vertical session can change a life, and Reuters notes that a year on, GameStop champion Roaring Kitty is quiet yet much richer [[n0496]]. The same anniversary coverage carries the sober half of the lesson: The Economist argues Wall Street was the real winner of the GameStop saga [[n0849]], and Business Insider counts $3.8 billion that US brokers made from payment for order flow amid the craze [[n0602]]. Mechanically, Snap is not a squeeze; it is an earnings gap in a stock priced for a Meta-style disaster. The overlap is behavioural: the money is made by whoever already holds when the gap opens, and late buyers inherit the volatility.
Smart Money View

Professional opinion splits along a data line. Barron's is constructive, framing Snap as free of the full Facebook problem set [[n0817]]. Reuters casts Meta's miss as a Big Tech divide over who's got the data [[n1113]], which cuts both ways for Snap: it is not Meta, but it cannot lean on the shopping and search data that shield the giants. Digiday's rundown that Google, Meta and Amazon are on track to absorb more than 50% of all ad money in 2022 [[n1154]] is the bear's reminder of how little room is left for the rest. Pinterest is the cautionary twin, with Social Media Today reporting its active users continue to slide as lockdown momentum fades [[n1116]]; an ad boom and user growth are different stories.
When the Narrative Breaks

Price gives the cleanest test. Snap's 38.91 USD close is still 6.65% below the 41.68 USD it fetched 20 sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), so the record day repaired damage rather than started a trend. If the first sessions after the gap hand back half of the 58.82% jump, the late buyers are trapped; a push through 41.68 USD would say the market is re-rating Snap, not just un-pricing a disaster. The macro trigger is rates: Reuters says the labor market shrugged off Omicron, leaving the economy strong ahead of rate hikes [[n2073]], and the Fed has pointed to a March hike [[n2089]], so the next inflation print can lift the discount rate under every long-duration growth story. The instrument risk is simple: short-dated calls bought after a 59% day price in volatility that has already happened.

retail.title: Peloton Interactive / PTON — the takeover lottery ticket
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Peloton is the purest lottery ticket on the board: a pandemic darling at 24.60 USD, down 27.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), suddenly wrapped in a takeover story. The Wall Street Journal reported that Amazon and other potential suitors are exploring a Peloton deal [[n0770]], the Guardian described Amazon as circling the exercise-bike maker as the company falters [[n0745]], and CNBC reported the stock surging on reports that Amazon and Nike are among potential buyers [[n0803]]. The story writes itself: the broken stock gets rescued by the biggest name in retail, no turnaround required, only a bid.
Where It Breaks

Exploring is not offering. Bloomberg warns a Peloton deal may pose a regulatory headache for a tech giant [[n0866]], the friction that turns a rumoured premium into a long wait. The 24.60 USD close on 4 February, up just 1.44%, is the anchor: if no named bidder appears and the shares drift back toward it, the premium was rented, not owned, and the company's next quarterly report becomes the real test of whether there is a business worth buying.

retail.title: Ford Motor / F — the EV dream at a discount
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Ford is the dip the EV crowd can afford. The shares fell 9.70% to 17.96 USD on Friday and are down 26.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), and Reuters notes they skidded despite a bullish 2022 outlook [[n0661]]. The story buy-the-dip believers tell is that the Mach-E maker is being priced like a chip-starved dinosaur: Reuters, citing Bloomberg News, reported Ford making a new investment of up to $20 billion in its EV push [[n0542]], and MotorTrend says Ford is going after dealers caught price-gouging as EV sales boom [[n1143]]. Demand outrunning supply is the problem dip-buyers like to own.
Where It Breaks

The discount has reasons. The Drive reports Ford slashing F-150, Bronco and Mustang Mach-E production because of the chip shortage [[n1160]], and Reuters says automakers and chip firms differ on when that shortage will abate [[n1134]]. The headline profit also leaned on a mark: the New York Times notes 2021 earnings of $17.9 billion were bolstered by a large gain on the Rivian stake [[n0660]], and Rivian sits at 60.87 USD after a 30.30% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Until production guidance stops slipping, every bounce is a trade, not a turnaround.

retail.title: MicroStrategy / MSTR — Saylor's leveraged ticket on the crypto bounce
parts: Why Retail Is Here

For the crypto crowd, the January flush is over. Al Jazeera reported that Bitcoin jumped 10% and climbed past $40,000 for the first time in two weeks [[n0945]], and Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 42,412.43 USD, up 9.47% over five days (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-06). The equity vehicles moved harder: MicroStrategy rose 15.16% to 391.64 USD, Grayscale Bitcoin Trust 13.52% and Riot Blockchain 12.04% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04). Michael Saylor's line that clear crypto regulations would speed institutional adoption [[n0510]] and Fundstrat's call for Bitcoin to $200k [[n0947]] supply the faith.
Where It Breaks

MicroStrategy is a leveraged proxy, and leverage cuts both ways: even after Friday it is down 21.46% over 20 sessions from 498.62 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04), while Bitcoin is just 0.38% above its level 20 days earlier. A daily close back under $40,000, the line Al Jazeera marked as reclaimed [[n0945]], would end the comeback story. Security risk is live, with CNBC reporting more than $320 million stolen in the latest apparent crypto hack [[n0923]], and a UN report, per the BBC, that stolen crypto funds North Korea's missile programme [[n1413]] invites a regulatory bite.
